about: The one curated source for where the Tear program stands. docs/POSITION.md is rendered from this file by `pnpm position:render`, and `pnpm check:docs` fails when the rendered file is stale or was edited by hand. Each area records its state in a few words, what is true now, the next step, what only the owner can do, and evidence: repository paths that exist, or links to pull requests. Change this file in the same pull request that changes an area's state, update `curated` when you review the whole file, and re-render.

areas.name: Verdant Sanctum visuals
areas.summary: The game draws Verdant itself at load from a stage art recipe (src/presentation/stage-art): a key light, an atmosphere, colour ramps and layers of shared strokes (foliage, trunks, ruined arcades, water, light), painted in short slices into layers the scene renderer composes. The painted image package is gone. Any biome reaches the same look with a recipe; Pale Traverse is next. Boss warnings and strikes on Verdant are drawn as roots and thorns rising from the floor, from a table on the stage's presentation definition that any biome can supply. The background does not move yet.
areas.next: Keep closing the look toward the owner's reference illustration, then a live layer (light shafts, water glints, sway) as recipe data, then Pale Traverse from a recipe.
areas.owner_action: Judge the drawn look against the reference illustration: the owner's taste decides visual work.

areas.name: Verdant Sanctum gameplay
areas.summary: The Rootbound boss is rebuilt in all three phases as data on a shared boss move layer that Pale and later bosses reuse: Phase I's moves, Phase II's Grafts, Root Cage and Bloom Wells, and Phase III's Regrowth and Last Spring. Its body no longer hurts on touch: it blocks, and it does not play a move the player could not walk out of. The stage's Bloom Wells stand on the floor and lift the player and light enemies; who a stage field moves is one data row. The Rootbinder is rebuilt as a support that backs away, plants and roots the allies near it, so they cannot be flung or lifted until the root is cut; cutting every root or one heavy hit uproots it, and it takes more damage while planted. Its old leash on the player is replaced by a warned snare: a ring marked on the ground that holds a player who stays in it, with a cut, a 2 second release and an immunity afterwards. Verdant's nine waves are written: each has listed enemies in spawn order (wave 32 two ground allies and then a Rootbinder, 33 a Mender, 36 a Chimera, 38 a second Rootbinder late) and the pool fills the rest; any stage can carry such a table. Their numbers are not tuned yet.
areas.next: Tune the waves against the playtest tool's wave measurements, then close Verdant.
areas.owner_action: Playtest the Rootbound in all three phases.

areas.name: Playtest tool
areas.state: Stage 1 done: pnpm playtest bosses prints a table per boss fight and phase; pnpm playtest sweep plays every boss, weapon, Easy and Normal with six scripted players and prints a summary
areas.summary: One command, pnpm playtest, that plays the game headless with scripted players on fixed seeds and reports clear rates, time to kill, damage taken and differences between builds. It is built from the working parts of TearBench and the scripted player and replaces both names. Verified on 2026-11-16: the scripted player runs headless at 13 to 15 times real time and the same seed reproduces exactly.
areas.next: Stage 2: every boss phase, wave and enemy kind as a row that starts directly, and pnpm playtest runs.

areas.name: Replays
areas.state: In progress: PR 1 and PR 2 merged (hidden replay features and replay extras removed); PR 2b open (REPAIR)
areas.summary: Players reach two replay systems today: Ghost 2 (position samples in localStorage, used by the REPLAYS tab, the feed and leaderboard links) and the Ghost V3 capsules (re-simulated, in IndexedDB, used by VAULT, CAREER and the Theater). The plan replaces both with one versioned record and five plain modules (record, store, watch, share, verify), moves the replay world and snapshot codecs out of TearBench, and deletes src/ghost (118 replay modules and about 800,000 characters today).
areas.next: Merge PR 2b, then PR 3 (the snapshot codecs move to src/gameplay/snapshot).

areas.name: Mobile, touch and phone layouts
areas.state: Paused by the owner 2026-11-19; out of the release builds
areas.summary: The owner paused all mobile work. The release builds (standalone, CrazyGames, itch) leave out the touch controls, the rotate gate, the phone profile layout and haptics, and a build check fails if they come back; a touch-only phone sees one line saying TEAR is played on a computer for now. Dev and test builds keep everything. The phone browser checks are parked in the mobile group (pnpm check:mobile). Touch-aim fixes are parked as draft pull request 191. Sessions write anything mobile will need later in plans/MOBILE_LATER.md.
